steps: Location, codes & floor

Install to CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes; in Massachusetts only a licensed plumber and gas fitter may install it. Peninsula wall, island or between two interior walls, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies.

Installation and venting must conform to the current CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or National Fuel Gas Code ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes, by qualified (licensed or trained) personnel.

  • Massachusetts: licensed plumber and gas fitter only. Where a sidewall exhaust terminal is less than seven (7) feet above finished grade, 248 CMR 5.08 carbon monoxide detector and signage rules apply (p. 4).
  • On carpeting, tile or other combustible material other than wood flooring, install on a metal or wood panel extending the full width and depth of the appliance (p. 9).
  • Manufactured (mobile) homes: after the "first sale" where local codes allow; the fireplace must be fastened in place (CAN/CSA Z240 MH; Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 or ANSI/NFPA 501A) (p. 7).
  • Must not be connected to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.
  • Equipped for altitudes 0 - 4500 ft. (0 - 1372 m) (rating label, p. 53).
Set the unit & fit the framing kit

Put the fireplace in its final location and install the venting before framing. The supplied steel stud framing kit (the top and side standoffs, 1-1/2" of depth adjustment) must be used unless the unit is totally enclosed in non-combustible material; bend the tabs out 90 degrees and fasten through them to the wood framing.

• The framing kit comes fully assembled and the outdoor section comes fully insulated. Frame the sides and top up to the steel studs with conventional lumber.
  • Loosen the mounting-bracket screws and set the depth before framing, then adjust to sit flush with the framing.
  • Do not insulate or use plastic vapour barrier within the framing kit. Against a non-insulated exterior wall or chase, insulate the outer walls like other exterior walls, cover insulation and vapour barrier with a solid surface such as drywall, and don't place the fireplace directly against the insulation (p. 9).
  • Seal the chase at the ceiling level or between floors in a multilevel installation.
  • Framing dimensions are a drawing: Figure 17, p. 13 (overall dimensions: Figure 1, p. 5).
Seal the outdoor wall

Straight Flash is factory installed over the stainless steel flanges; overlap and seal the house wrap to it. Any siding rated 120 F minimum may be used, but it must stay off the removable outer door trim and leave a 1 1/2" air space below the door frame for ventilation.

• Outdoor side order of assembly: inner trim, glass assembly, outer trim (Figure 9, p. 9). A 1/2" OSB board is factory installed (Figure 10, p. 10).
  • Siding or facing may touch the top and sides of the door frame but not the bottom, and must not contact the removable outer window trim; leave enough space to remove the trim.
  • Keep a minimum 1 1/2 inch space between the bottom of the door frame and the siding. Facing above or below that space may extend outward as far as desired as long as the space is maintained.
  • House wrap overlaps and is sealed to the Straight Flash as per local/national building codes (p. 12).
Non-combustible facing & lintel

Sheet the front in non-combustible backer board (cement board or equivalent) up to the top of the metal frame and out to the framing edge bars; standard drywall may be used beyond. Recess up to 4 1/2" in non-combustible material only, and set the adjustable lintel flush with the facing.

• A 3/4" facing finishes flush with the unit front; additional masonry-type non-combustible material may sit above and to the sides up to 4 1/2 inches forward of the appliance.
  • No building material may protrude past the lintel bars; the space between the outside lintels and the firebox stays free of obstructions, and the door with trim must move freely. Finishes must not stop the glass door opening in the event of ignition of excess gas buildup.
  • If the board isn't finished with other non-combustible material such as tile, make its top sections a single sheet of calcium silicate board (1/2" thick); taped and mudded joints may crack. To paint the wall above, discard the framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board with full length metal studs.
  • Pre-drill the board and fasten it with drywall screws; don't use cracked board.
  • Lintel: ships flange edge out. To switch to the hemmed edge, remove the safety barrier screen and door trim, loosen the securing bolts in the upper and lower corners on each side, rotate it, slide in or out approximately 1" to align with the facing, tighten, then refit the trim and screen.
Power, controls & wall switch

Connect 110 V. AC to the wires in the junction box and make sure the IFC board's NV/PV switch is set to PV. Run the supplied 40 ft communication cable to the wall switch in the same room (use the entire length, no substitute or add-on), leave the wall switch battery holder empty, and link the remote.

• Access: remove the glass door and the firebox access panel; the junction box wires can be reached through either of its two small access panels.
  • Link the remote: selector toggle to REMOTE, press the internal PROGRAM button once with a straightened paper clip, wait for 3 beeps from the wall switch, then press the remote's ON/OFF; the wall unit beeps 3 times when it's programmed. Keep the toggle on REMOTE to use the remote.
  • Home automation: dry contact relay for flame and light on/off; 0 - 10 volt DC analog input for flame and light level (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts); cable to the wall switch no more than 200 feet. Leave the wall switch on Remote. The control repeats a signal every 2 hours or until a new command arrives (p. 19).
  • No rheostat on the supply voltage. Wire to CSA C22.2 (Canada) or ANSI/NFPA 70 (U.S.) and local codes (p. 21).
  • Start-up check: with gas and power on, move the wall control's center button to ON. The igniter sparks; after a short delay the pilot lights, followed by the main burner.
Gas supply & leak test

Supply line access holes are beneath the fireplace on the flue side of the control box; the valve inlet accepts a 3/8" N.P.T. fitting. Install a drip leg and a union or flanged connection just upstream of the valve inside the control compartment, connect to the gas connector and check that all connections are tight and leak free.

• Use the correct gas line diameter to assure proper operation and pressure.
  • Disconnect the appliance and its shut off valve from the supply piping for pressure tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); close its manual shut off valve for tests at or below 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa) (p. 3).
  • Reinstall the access panel and its gasket after installation, conversion or servicing; leaving it off overheats the control system and causes premature failure.
  • Warranty condition: sediment traps must be installed within 6 feet of the gas control valve (Owner's Manual p. 15).
Power vent system

A power vent is mandatory and the flue collar takes 5" x 8" pipe only. Horizontal runs use power vent unit #22270004 with its internal fan on HIGH; vertical runs use #22270013. Stay within 110' total and a 66' vertical rise, seal every outer joint with the supplied high temperature aluminium tape and support the pipe at least every 4'.

Venting variables (p. 22): any combination of rise and run up to 110' including up to 3 ft below the unit; six 90-degree elbows (or equivalent) max, deducting 2' per 90-degree turn; minimum 3 ft plus one 90-degree elbow. The inner pipe does not need to be sealed (p. 25).

Vent terminal minimum clearances (p. 23)

C · permanently closed window (recommended)12 inches (30 cm)
D · ventilated soffit within 2 feet (60 cm)24 inches (60 cm)

Burner kit (convert to LP first)

Remove the red silicone cap from the vacuum tube in the bulkhead plate, then install the Tranquility or Twilight Diamond burner kit and the firebox side panels. Set both air shutters the same (fully closed for natural gas, 13/64 (0.2)" open for LP) and butt the burners tightly together at the center.

Propane conversion (kit # TCWS54ST_D.LP, pp. 32–33)

  1. Shut off the gas supply and electrical power. Remove any sand and rocks, the burner tray (8 screws) and the burners.
  2. Remove the access panel beneath the burners to reach the gas valve motor head stepper motor; convert it per the SIT conversion kit instruction book.
  3. With a 1/2" wrench, replace the natural gas orifice (marked #32) with the propane orifice (marked #51), using a small amount of pipe joint compound on the threads.
  4. Open each primary air shutter to a gap of 13/64" (0.2").
  5. Loosen the pilot head (7/16" wrench) and slide the pilot adjustment band to the LP position.
  6. Fill in the conversion label and apply it over the gas specifications on the rating label. Reinstall the access panel and control box shield, then confirm manifold pressure.

Factory supplied components must be used. Twilight Diamond lights: route the floor-plate wires through the grommets into the electrical connection box and connect them to a switched 120 VAC, 60Hz, 3A supply (p. 40). Stop for the gas pressure check before installing the burner tray and media.
Gas pressure check & flame

Before the tray and media go in: turn off the gas, open the test port (3/16" hex key) next to the center tray leg, fit the extension test fitting and a gauge, and verify pressure with the fireplace lit on its highest setting. Then set the air shutter for a flame that is just orange and "lazy", never sooting.

NG supply min / max5.0" WC / 13.9" WC
LP supply min / max12.5" WC / 13.9" WC
NG manifold max / min3.5" WC / 1.6" WC
LP manifold max / min10" WC / 6.4" WC

Rest the gauge on the secondary floor where it's visible with the doors closed and the unit running. When done, shut off the gas, remove the fitting and replace the plug with thread sealant. Evaluate the flame once the fireplace reaches operating temperature: open primary air if the door glass and firebox collect carbon or the flames are long, dark and stringy (opening it also lessens flame height).
Media, trim & safety screen

Install the burner tray and media (sand, rocks and pilot rock, or glass over the mesh) and the porcelain strips with the narrow edge toward the center. Refit the door, add the indoor-side Finishing Touch trim kit and the magnetic safety barrier screen, then light the fireplace per the lighting instructions.

• Tranquility: tray with 8 screws (around the pilot first); sand brushed smooth and kept away from the burner ports; lettered rocks with their arrows all facing the same way, placed from the outdoor side starting at the right; repeat the set three more times, place the fifth set at random, and set the pilot rock with its opening toward the burner center (pp. 29–31).
  • Twilight Diamond: mesh tray screwed to the panels (two per side) and to the burners (8 per burner); spread the glass media evenly, keeping the protrusion above the pilot clear (pp. 36–37).
  • Door frame: two spring-loaded latches on a one-piece handle; the handle should snap in flush. To check the latch, pull the top corners of the frame forward; it should return evenly on both sides (p. 7).
  • Trim kit (indoor side only): side pieces on the small button magnets, top piece on the larger magnets, meshed bottom piece on the floor between the outer-most door frame and the glass; badge on the right side of the lower piece (pp. 38–39).

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
An igniter lights the pilot for you, then the main burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Turn it on

  1. First, smell all around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow Safety & gas smell.
  2. Push the On/Off switch to ON. On the wall switch, that means moving the center button to ON. Or, with the wall switch set to REMOTE, press ON/OFF on the remote.
  3. Give it up to 30 seconds to ignite. The igniter sparks, the pilot lights, and then the burner.
  4. Set the flame you want with the hand-held remote.

If it doesn't light

Push the switch to OFF and wait at least 5 minutes for any gas to clear. Still smell gas? Stop. No smell? Try again. If it won't light or stay lit after several tries, switch it OFF, turn off all electric power to the fireplace and call your service technician or gas supplier.

The very first time it's lit, it needs extra time for air to clear out of the gas lines.

Turn it off

Push the On/Off switch to Off. For service or a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power to the fireplace.

remote.title: Using the Proflame 2 remote
remote.html:
The remote runs on 3 AAA batteries. Keep the wall switch set to REMOTE so the remote can work. The fireplace answers each command with a single beep.

ON/OFF keyturns the fireplace on or off
Up / Down arrowssix flame levels, down to flame off
Mode key to the bulb iconlight dimmer, six levels (Up / Down)
Mode + Up togetherkey lock on or off

If you press Up while the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the flame comes back on high. Key lock stops unsupervised use.

Pilot mode: IPI or CPI

The control can run an intermittent pilot (IPI) or a continuous pilot (CPI). With the system off, press Mode until the CPI icon shows. Press Up for CPI, or Down to go back to IPI.

Thermostat

The remote has a room thermostat function, but it's disabled by default. The manual says thermostat use isn't permissible in the USA (it is in Canada).

If the remote stops working or its batteries die, turn the fireplace off with the on/off switch on the wall. Pairing a new remote is covered under Pair the remote & TC Fire app.

firstfire.title: First fire: what's normal
firstfire.html:
A smell for the first couple of hours

The first time it's lit, the fireplace gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours while paints, sealants and lubricants from manufacturing cure. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room. The odor can bother some people.

Ticks and creaks

Steel fireplaces make some expansion and contraction noises as they heat up and cool down. Your furnace's heat exchanger and your oven do the same.

A short wait to light

It can take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time you turn it on. The very first lighting takes longer while air clears from the gas lines.

Beeps

A single beep from the fireplace means it received a command from your remote.

A gas smell is different. If you smell gas, don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbour's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass as needed with fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Never clean the glass while it's hot. Turn the fireplace off and let it cool first.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners on the glass or any other part of the fireplace.
  • Don't strike or knock the glass. The ceramic glass is very fragile.
  • Clean the fireplace's exterior finish with mild soap and water.
Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

If the glass cracks or breaks

Don't use the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. It must be replaced first, by a licensed or qualified service person, with ceramic glass only, from your Town & Country dealer.

Note: the owner's manual gives the replacement glass size as 52" x 42" x 5mm (p. 11), and the installation manual gives 52" x 16-1/4" x 5mm (p. 46).

app.title: Pairing the remote and the TC Fire app
app.html:
Besides the wall switch and remote, you can run the fireplace from an Apple (iOS) device over Bluetooth with the free TC Fire app. Link things in this order.

1. Wall switch to fireplace

  1. Set the wall switch selector to Remote.
  2. With a straightened paper clip, press and hold the Program button for up to 10 seconds. The wall switch beeps 5 times; let go.
  3. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more. They're linked.

2. Remote to wall switch

  1. Press and release Program once. The wall switch beeps 3 times.
  2. Within 60 seconds, press and release ON/OFF on the remote. The wall switch beeps 3 times and the remote is ready.

3. TC Fire app (optional)

Download TC Fire from the Apple App Store. Open Add/Edit Fireplace, press Add, enter the PIN from the sticker on the wall switch and a name for the fireplace, then press Save. Toggles turn the flame and lighting on and off; sliders set their levels.

If a nearby fireplace turns on instead of yours, repeat step 1. It moves to another of three channels.
Note: the owner's manual describes the pairing beeps two ways: on p. 13 the wall switch beeps 3 times when the remote is linked; on p. 7 the remote itself beeps 4 times when it's synchronized.

power.title: Power and batteries
power.html:
This fireplace runs on house power. Its control module is powered by AC power only and doesn't use battery backup.

Wall switch battery holderleave it empty
Remote3 AAA batteries
  • When the remote's batteries run low, a low-battery icon appears on its screen before the power is gone. It disappears once you replace them.
  • Turn off the main gas supply to the fireplace before you remove or reinsert batteries.
  • Remote dead? The on/off switch on the wall switch turns the fireplace off and bypasses the remote.
  • For maintenance, turn the fireplace off at the wall switch and at its circuit breaker.
Note: the owner's manual (p. 7) and installation manual (p. 18) say the wall switch must not have batteries and the fireplace must not operate on battery backup; the owner's manual also describes a low-battery double-beep from the control module (p. 10), and the lighting label says to remove backup batteries for service (p. 4).

house.title: Indoor-outdoor basics
house.html:
Your fireplace is see-through: one side faces your room, the other faces outdoors through the exterior wall.

Decorative, not a heater

The manual calls it a decorative product that isn't intended to be used as a heating appliance. It's suitable for a bedroom or bed-sitting room.

How it insulates the wall

Town & Country rates the fireplace at an R value of 5.8. That's calculated from two layers of 5mm ceramic glass combined with 17 inches of ventilated air gap. A third layer, 5mm tempered glass, isn't counted because it's open to the outside air on both sides. Real-world results may vary.

Good to know

  • Use it only with the glass and screen barrier certified with it.
  • Outdoors, a 1 1/2 inch air space under the outer door frame is required for ventilation.
  • Clean the exterior finish with mild soap and water, never abrasive cleaners.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The barrier that came with the fireplace reduces the risk of burns from the hot glass. It must be installed to protect children and other at-risk people.
  • Supervise young children in the room. An adjustable safety gate can keep toddlers and other at-risk people away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies, gasoline and other flammable liquids away.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob, and never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician right away to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
  • Put back any panel, grill or door removed for service before you use it.

service.title: The yearly inspection
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the fireplace and its venting at least once a year. Before any service, the gas and electrical power are turned off and the fireplace is left to cool.

What the yearly check covers

  • Removing the glass and checking the burner media for soot. Heavy soot means the unit needs to be inspected and adjusted for proper combustion.
  • Cleaning the media and the burner, paying close attention to the burner ports.
  • Checking the pilot's flame size and operation, and cleaning the pilot.
  • Making sure the vent pipe and vent terminal are open and free of blockage or debris.
  • Checking the glass gasket and replacing it if needed. A good glass seal matters.
  • Checking and replacing batteries as needed.
More frequent cleaning may be needed if there's a lot of lint from carpet or bedding. Keep the control compartment, burner and air passageways clean, and keep the area around the fireplace clear of combustible materials and flammable liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Town & Country's Limited Lifetime Warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Glass (thermal breakage only)limited lifetime, parts only
Combustion chamberlimited lifetime, parts only
Burner tube assemblylimited lifetime, parts only
Porcelain finisheslimited lifetime, parts only
Any defective parttwo years, parts and labor

Conditions worth knowing

  • A qualified technician must install it, following the appliance manual and local and national requirements.
  • Sediment traps must be installed within 6 feet of the gas control valve.
  • Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention. Some colors darken when hot and return to their shade when cool.

Not covered

  • Parts showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
Any installation or operating deviation from the manual's instructions voids the warranty. This is a summary; the full terms are in the owner's manual.

specFrame.title: Framing, finishing & the outdoor wall
specFrame.html:
Framing kitsteel studs, supplied · top & side standoffs
Framing kit depth adjustment1-1/2"
Non-combustible recess4 1/2" max.
Facing for a flush finish3/4" thick
Lintel slideapproximately 1" in or out
Calcium silicate board1/2" thick
Outdoor sidingminimum 120 F rating
Air space below outer door frame1 1/2 inch min.

Set the unit in its final location (venting installed) before framing. Framing and overall dimensions are drawings (Figure 17, p. 13; Figure 1, p. 5). Non-combustible backer board such as cement board must extend to the top of the metal frame and out to the framing edge bars; nothing may protrude past the lintel bars, and finishing material must not interfere with glass frame access. If the wall above will be painted, discard the framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board with full length metal studs.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Fireplace110 volts, 60Hz, 0.25A
Power vent kit (p. 17)115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A
Blower rating (rating label)115v, 60hz, 1.1 A
Twilight burner lightsswitched 120 VAC, 60Hz, 3A supply
Wall switch cable40 ft, supplied
Home automation cableno more than 200 feet to the wall switch

Connect 110 V. AC to the wires in the junction box. Use the entire supplied communication cable, with no substitute or add-on, and mount the wall switch in the same room as the fireplace. A power vent is mandatory on this fireplace, so set the IFC board's NV/PV switch to PV. No batteries in the wall switch: this fireplace must not operate on battery backup. Never use a rheostat to alter the supply voltage.

Note: p. 17 rates the power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label (p. 53) gives a blower electrical rating of 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A.
p. 17 calls it the "optional power vent kit"; pp. 16 and 22 say a power vent is mandatory on this fireplace, p. 18 says the NV/PV switch must be set to PV in all cases, and the rating label (p. 53) lists the power vent kit as a required component.

conflicts.issue: Propane input: the rating label gives LP Max.: 54,900 (16.0) / Min.: 45,000 (13.2) BTU/hr (kW); the LP conversion label reproduced in the conversion instructions gives Max.: 62,000Btu (18.1kw) / Min.: 49,000Btu (14.3kw).

Vent pipe clearance: the minimum clearance list (p. 6) gives 1 3/4" in. (45 mm) and the rating label (p. 53) 1.75 in. (45 mm); the venting section (p. 21) says no combustible closer than 1 1/2 inches to any part of the venting pipe and lists vertical pipe 1.5 in. (38 mm), horizontal pipe 4 in. (100mm) above and 2 in. (50mm) to the sides and under. Also flagged in specVent.
Replacement glass size: the owner's manual says 52" x 42" x 5mm; the installation manual says 52" x 16-1/4" x 5mm.

Power vent called the 'optional power vent kit' on p. 17, but p. 16 and p. 22 say a power vent is mandatory on this indoor/outdoor fireplace, the cover says 'Power vented only' and the rating label lists the power vent kit under required components.
conflicts.corrected_to: mandatory (pp. 16, 18 and 22; cover: Power vented only; rating label p. 53 lists the power vent kit as a required component)

conflicts.issue: Vent fan electrical rating: p. 17 rates the power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label lists a blower electrical rating of 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A (no other blower is described for this model).

Battery backup: the owner's manual (p. 7) and installation manual (pp. 17-18) say no batteries in the wall switch, the IFC module runs on AC power only and the fireplace must not operate on battery backup; the owner's manual's Low Battery Power Detection (p. 10) describes an IFC-module low-battery double-beep, and the lighting label (doc 2 p. 4 / doc 1 p. 45) says to remove backup batteries for service or extended shutdown.

Remote pairing confirmation: Initializing (owner's manual p. 7) says the IFC module beeps 3 times after Program and the remote beeps 4 times when synchronized; the linking procedure (owner's manual p. 13) and the installation manual (p. 18) say the wall switch beeps 3 times after Program and again 3 times when the remote is linked.

review.notes: Both manuals have clean text layers and their footer page numbers match the physical pages (the doc 1 table of contents runs one page high from p. 11 on). Efficiency matches the catalog (P.4.1-15 Efficiency: 30.7%, p. 53); the catalog view area (748 sq in) and catalog features such as the 316 marine-grade surround, cool-glass and LED lighting are not stated in the manual text, so they were not checked. Figure-only content pointed to instead of transcribed: overall dimensions (Fig. 1 p. 5; Fig. 13 p. 12 shows 54 1/16" and 74 3/4" with no axis labels), framing dimensions (Fig. 17 p. 13: 54-1/4", 75", 19-1/2" - 21"), the lettered mantel clearance/depth chart (Fig. 2 p. 6; the guide gives only the rating label's 9 in. / 12 in.), columns B and C of the minimum vent length chart (Fig. 36 p. 23; only the labelled 58 7/16" floor-to-flue-center rise is used), rock placement photos (pp. 30-31) and the wiring diagrams (pp. 41, 52); pp. 54-55 carry no text. No troubleshooting chart or code table: the fault panels are built from Burner Flame Adjustment (doc 1 p. 43), the lighting label (doc 1 p. 45 / doc 2 p. 4), the annual inspection (doc 1 p. 46), the wall switch note (doc 1 p. 18) and the owner's manual remote and pairing text (doc 2 pp. 5, 6, 8, 10, 12); codes left empty because beep signals are not a code table. p. 17 puts the gas control system on the 'right hand side' of the firebox but the access panel at the 'bottom left hand side'; on a see-through unit this may depend on the viewing side, so the guide avoids left/right. Power vent part numbers come from two systems: p. 16 names units #22270004 (horizontal) and #22270013 (vertical); the rating label lists TCVT.PV7.110, TCVT.PVCV, TCVT.PVVT. Both are given as printed, not mapped to each other. LP orifice: the text says the propane orifice is marked #51, while Fig. 65 and the conversion label print 1.78 mm (P/N 5022.72); the guide gives only the #32/#51 markings. Part-number oddities not used in the guide: the Twilight Diamond insert sheet (p. 34) is for TCWS.54NG03C2 Series C2 while the parts list (p. 50) gives TCWS.54NGST03D; the parts page is titled TCWS.54DST. The owner's manual's Proflame 2 description mentions a six-speed comfort fan and an auxiliary outlet (doc 2 p. 7); no fan is described for this model, so the guide doesn't mention one. The thermostat is disabled by default and 'not permissible in the USA' (doc 2 p. 6); the Canadian enabling procedure (doc 2 p. 9) is left out. Title is 34 characters so it stays distinct from the indoor WS54 See-Thru guide.
